Ranked below Site 1 because electrophysiological function was not cleanly measured for the BBS-tagged construct alone. sources.claim: HERG1a-YFP was generated by using overlap extension polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to fuse YFP in frame to the C terminus of hERG1a, as described previously. 39 Sequence for a BBS (13 amino acid residues) was placed between residues Thr436 and Glu437 in the hERG1a extracellular S1–S2 loop using the Quik-Change Lightning site-directed mutagenesis kit (Stratagene) to generate BBS-hERG1a-YFP.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: yes — electrophysiological properties explicitly stated to be unaffected by the tag; surface display confirmed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy in non-permeabilized HEK293 cells
sites.rationale: Highest-confidence site: exact junction validated by published HA-tag insertion in full-length surface-expressed KCNH2, with both surface display and preserved electrophysiology confirmed. The 17-aa tag (within the 13-23 aa range) sits in the middle of the 24-aa S1-S2 loop, well clear of TM boundaries and the C445-C449 disulfide pair. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A previously published 34 9 amino acid HA tag with surrounding 4 amino acid linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE) was inserted between amino acids T443 and E444 (in the extracellular region between the S1 and S2 helices) by inverse PCR 35 (Table S1).
